**Liverpool host Manchester City at Anfield on Saturday, October 10, 2026 (15:00 UK kickoff), in Matchweek 7 or 8 of the 2026-27 Premier League season.**[[1]](https://www.facebook.com/groups/1095209774752633/posts/2082949352645332/)[[2]](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7363576/2026/06/19/manchester-city-premier-league-fixtures-2026-27-schedule/)

This is the first of two league meetings that season (the return is at the Etihad on May 8, 2027). Fixtures were released in mid-June 2026, well before the August 15 cutoff.[[3]](https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/fixtures-202627-announced-premier-league-63917455)[[4]](https://www.balls.ie/football/liverpool-fixtures-2026-27-657736)

### Head-to-Head History
Liverpool hold a clear historical edge. Across 201 all-time meetings, Liverpool have 95 wins, City 53, and 53 draws. In Premier League games specifically, the record is more balanced but still favors Liverpool slightly in wins (around 21–23 vs. City’s 13–14, with many draws).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C.%E2%80%93Manchester_City_F.C._rivalry)[[6]](https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/man-city-vs-liverpool-history-181300346.html)

Since 1995 (64 games tracked in one source), Liverpool won 27, City 15, and there were 22 draws, with Liverpool scoring more goals overall (101–91).[[7]](https://m.aiscore.com/head-to-head/soccer-liverpool-vs-manchester-city)

Liverpool dominate at Anfield (strong home record in the fixture), while recent City home results against them had been strong in some periods (e.g., multiple wins by large margins in select seasons). No major tournament (e.g., Champions League or cups) meetings immediately relevant to the 2026-27 context were highlighted in pre-August sources beyond the general rivalry intensity that began intensifying in the mid-2010s.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C.%E2%80%93Manchester_City_F.C._rivalry)

### Recent Form and 2025-26 Context (Leading into 2026-27)
The 2025-26 season saw Manchester City experience a notable dip in 2026, including a midwinter slump with inconsistent results (e.g., multiple draws and losses amid heavy injury issues) after a stronger festive period. They were described as struggling for form and dealing with an extended injury crisis affecting key players.[[8]](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jan/21/what-exactly-is-going-wrong-at-manchester-city)[[9]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ovA1mcFmGvw)

Liverpool, under Arne Slot, maintained competitiveness but also faced significant injury disruptions by the end of 2025-26. Preseason friendlies for both teams occurred in July–August 2026 (e.g., Liverpool’s U.S. tour, City’s Hong Kong match and Community Shield), providing some preparation time before the new campaign.[[10]](https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49154575/premier-league-preseason-friendlies-202627-fixtures-uk-kickoff-s-summer-tour-schedule-chelsea-liverpool-arsenal-man-united-man-city-spurs)

### Injuries and Suspensions
Both squads carried notable injury concerns from the 2025-26 season into the summer of 2026, with limited full recoveries reported by early/mid-2026 sources:

- **Liverpool**: Long-term absences included Hugo Ekitike (ruptured Achilles, expected long recovery into 2026/27), Conor Bradley (knee), Giovanni Leoni (ACL/knee), Stefan Bajcetic (hamstring/ongoing), and others like Jayden Danns (thigh) and potential issues for players such as Alisson or Florian Wirtz in earlier updates. Multiple sources from May 2026 noted these as season-ending or extended.[[11]](https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/liverpools-injury-list-suspensions-and-availability)[[12]](https://www.nbcsports.com/soccer/news/premier-league-injury-table-2025-26-season-club-by-club-injuries-suspensions-latest-updates)
- **Manchester City**: Defensive and midfield injuries plagued them, including Joško Gvardiol (fractured tibia/leg, uncertain return), Rúben Dias (hamstring), John Stones (thigh/leg), Rodri (groin/knee recovery from prior long absence), Savinho (quad/knock), Mateo Kovačić (ankle/post-surgery), and others like Oscar Bobb. Some returns were targeted for early 2026, but the squad depth was stretched.[[8]](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jan/21/what-exactly-is-going-wrong-at-manchester-city)[[13]](https://www.facebook.com/richard.musyoki.336911/posts/-manchester-city-injury-update-as-of-january-28-2026heres-the-latest-rundown-of-/887422230814672/)

These lists reflect the situation as of mid-2026 sources; updates closer to October would depend on recoveries during the summer break and early season. ### Travel, Fatigue, Venue, and Other Factors
- **Travel and fatigue**: Minimal. Both clubs are based in the North West of England (Liverpool and Manchester are roughly 35–40 miles apart). The October 10 date follows the early international break window, potentially allowing recovery time, though any midweek European commitments could factor in. - **Venue (Anfield)**: Standard Premier League conditions—no altitude or extreme climate issues. Pitch is well-maintained. Liverpool’s home advantage is significant due to the intense atmosphere and vocal Anfield crowd, historically a factor in this fixture.[[14]](https://www.facebook.com/groups/3850570908307771/posts/26517822677822605/)
- **Other storylines**: This is a high-profile early-season clash between two traditional rivals, with title-race implications likely given both teams’ ambitions. Preseason narratives around squad rebuilding, managerial continuity (Slot at Liverpool, Guardiola at City), and integrating new signings or recovering players would have been prominent. No major off-field controversies or unique external factors (e.g., weather forecasts) were widely reported in pre-August coverage. All details above derive exclusively from sources published before August 15, 2026 (primarily June–July 2026 reports on fixtures, historical stats, and 2025-26 injury/form updates). Actual match outcomes or later developments are disregarded per the query constraints.

factors.impact: Liverpool holds a clear historical edge over Manchester City in overall meetings (95 wins vs 53), and a slight advantage in Premier League games. This long-standing pattern, especially strong at Anfield, suggests a historical difficulty for City in this fixture.

Liverpool has a historically dominant home record against Manchester City at Anfield. The intense atmosphere and vocal crowd are explicitly noted as significant factors in this rivalry, making it a challenging venue for visiting teams.

Man City experienced a notable dip in form and an extended injury crisis in early 2026, described as 'struggling for form' and dealing with 'inconsistent results' heading into the 2026-27 season. This suggests they may not be starting the season at peak performance.

Both Liverpool and Man City carried significant long-term injury concerns from the 2025-26 season into the summer of 2026. While the full extent of recovery by October 10 is uncertain, City's injury issues were notably linked to their prior season's dip in form and stretched squad depth in key defensive and midfield positions.

analysis.reasoning: Based on the pre-August 15, 2026 research notes, Liverpool is favored in this matchup. The primary drivers for this adjustment are Liverpool's consistently strong historical head-to-head record against Manchester City, particularly their dominance at Anfield, which is noted as a significant home advantage due to the intense crowd atmosphere. Furthermore, Manchester City concluded the 2025-26 season with a documented mid-winter slump and an extended injury crisis in early 2026, leading to a period of 'struggling for form' that could impact their readiness for the new campaign. While both teams faced significant injury disruptions heading into the summer, City's specific issues were explicitly tied to their prior performance dip and stretched squad depth. The early season timing (October 10) allows for some player recovery or integration, but the historical patterns and City's documented pre-season struggles provide a clear lean towards Liverpool.
